drawings.description: à gauche, un croquis de $\widetilde{X}$ : deux anneaux hachurés le long de deux composantes du bord, l'épaisseur de chacun marquée $\varepsilon_{i}$, et sous le dessin « $0 \leqslant \varepsilon_{i} < +\infty$ »
drawings.kind: surface with collars (annuli along boundary components)
drawings.notes: Two rings (annuli along two boundary components), each with hatching on part of the collar and a small epsilon_i marking its width; under them "0 <= epsilon_i < +infinity". The long faint ruled-looking strokes crossing the crop belong to the writing of the page and are left out, as is a small struck sign above the right ring.

drawings.description: à gauche, un croquis : une composante $(\partial'\widetilde{X})_{i}$ entourée d'une couronne hachurée, et dans celle-ci le cercle $\Gamma_{i}$
drawings.kind: boundary component with hatched collar
drawings.notes: Redrawn 2026-11-09 after Michel's check (#136) from a fresh crop of p. 3; the bbox is widened to take the hatching whole. Four closed hand-drawn curves, traced from the crop: the inner curve (the component); a curve round it, broken at the top where the label (d'X~)_i is written on it; a second closed curve that overlaps it, crossing it four times (its upper left side runs diagonally inside the first, its top and bottom run outside it, its right side inside it; this is the closed line the earlier redraw had split into two open pieces and a wrong closed curve); and the outer closed curve, with the short stroke where its pen line ends at the bottom right. The hatching of the collar, as the transcription says: thirteen pieces of long parallel oblique strokes, drawn grey, which run across the figure and out beyond it on both sides, stopping at the middle curves so that the region round the component is left blank (the topmost stroke and the long one through the top of the outer curve, and the lowest one, are whole). Labels \small: (d'X~)_i at the top, Gamma_i at the bottom left between the two middle curves. Left out: the small ticks where a hatching stroke meets a curve, the text around the figure. Still to settle (not asked in #136): which of the two middle curves is Gamma_i. Redrawn 2026-11-09: to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the label Gamma_i is written at the lower left between the two middle curves, beside a small tick on them, and the redraw places it there; which of the two overlapping middle curves he means does not change the figure (both are closed curves in the collar round the component, drawn as on the page), so the question is closed without change. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan (250 ppi native) on a unit grid; the component, the two middle curves, the outer curve of the collar and the long oblique hatching strokes lie on their ink to within 1 to 2 units, as found on 12 November, so the redraw is unchanged. Not compiled (no TeX in the session). 2026-11-14, Claude Opus 5.5, issue 147 second pass: the small ticks where hatching strokes meet the curves, the short heavier inked marks on the curves, the hook at the start of the inner curve's upper left, the heavy stretch of the inner curve at its upper right and the two dots, all left out before, drawn stroke by stroke where they stand, read on a contrast-raised crop of the 400 dpi colour scan at 24 pixels per unit. Overlay with the local TikZ interpreter (not compiled: no TeX in the session): the curves, hatching strokes, ticks and marks lie on their ink to within about one unit.

drawings.description: à gauche, trois croquis de cylindres traversés de cercles et de courbes, le troisième biffé
drawings.kind: cylinders crossed by circles and curves
drawings.notes: Two pencil cylinders, each between two horizontal lines and crossed by three closed curves. Omitted as struck: the third cylinder (bottom left), struck through by oblique strokes. The marginal words on the right ("cylindre ...") are left out. Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: feuillet de croquis, formules éparses et dessins dans tous les sens ; on n'en donne que les formules
drawings.kind: page of sketches (surfaces, pants, spheres)
drawings.notes: Whole page, drawn upright as rendered (the formulas, written upside down, are left out: they are in the transcription). Top: a Y-shaped piece (pair of pants, heavy stem, doubled arms) with a heavy bar under it; a small circle on a doubled stalk; a thin crescent; a large circle drawn twice over, with a short tail. Middle: faint pencil hills (the left one, a larger one) on a base line, with three short strokes at their right (pencil). Long thin lines: one from the small circle down to the lower right (with a bend where it crosses the step line), one parallel to it from the middle left down to the bottom, a third further left, and a faint line rising to the right under the formula. Lower half: the long ink line with its step, the shorter line under it; the blob with three crescents and a small loop, and its lower loop; the heavy vertical stroke under it; a sphere with two meridian arcs at the right. Left out: all formulas and words, the faint pencil writing at the lower left, the strokes underlining the formulas at the bottom right. Still differs: the faint pencil hills and the blob with its crescents are approximate. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan (250 ppi native) on a unit grid; the drawn sketches (the Y-shaped piece, the small and large circles, the long lines, the step line, the blob with its loops, the sphere at the right) lie on their ink to within 1 to 2 units, so the redraw is unchanged. Not compiled (no TeX in the session). Still differs, as before: the faint pencil hills and the blob with its crescents are approximate (2 to 3 units in places); the formulas, written in all directions, are left out, as the transcription carries them.

drawings.description: sur une enveloppe, un croquis sans légende : un grand disque contenant un disque plus petit autour d'un point marqué, et deux petits disques cerclés autour de deux autres points ; à côté, un second contour fermé avec un point
drawings.kind: discs with marked points
drawings.notes: On the envelope: a closed contour with one point (top), and a large disc containing a smaller disc around a marked point, and two small ringed points (bottom). The printed address and the handwritten name on the envelope are outside the crop and left out.

drawings.description: en bas à droite, un croquis : une sphère, $z$ au pôle nord, $z'$ au pôle sud, quelques méridiens et un point marqué $x$
drawings.kind: sphere with poles and meridians
drawings.notes: The sphere as he drew it (an irregular closed outline through both poles), z at the north pole (heavy point) and z' at the south pole (small ring); a meridian from z curving down the middle to z'; a heavy line from z down to the lower left; a curve from the upper right down towards the centre; the equator-like curve from the left edge to the right edge; a short stroke from the right end of that curve downwards; oblique strokes over the left part (his hatching); a short stroke right of z'. Earlier: no point labelled x was found (settled 2026-11-12, below); the small dashes inside the sphere were left out (drawn on 2026-11-14). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): at 600 dpi a small x-shaped mark stands inside the sphere at the upper right, just right of z, where the curve from the upper right begins: it is the x of the transcription, and the redraw now carries the letter x there (no dot is drawn, the page has none; a small loop of the pen lower on the same curve is not drawn). Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-14, Claude Opus 5.5, issue 147 second pass: redrawn stroke by stroke from the 400 dpi colour scan on a gridded crop at 22 pixels per unit: the long oblique strokes on the left are the page's two separate strokes from the top (the earlier redraw had joined pieces of them), with the extra stroke inside the left of the outline where he went over it; the small tick above the sphere; the small dashes and marks inside the sphere (about a dozen), each where it stands; the short stroke from x towards the upper right, the curved stroke at the right above the horizontal curve, the second short stroke beside the right meridian and the small loop of the pen on it; the lower end of the heavy line moved onto its ink. Overlay with the local TikZ interpreter (not compiled: no TeX in the session): every stroke, both points and the letters lie on their ink to within about one unit.

drawings.description: en marge du dernier alinéa, un croquis : un demi-disque dont le diamètre porte un point marqué.
drawings.kind: half-disc with a marked point
drawings.notes: A half-disc; the diameter carries a marked point, and its right end is overinked.

drawings.description: au crayon, sur la moitié droite du feuillet (tenu dans le sens de son écriture), trois croquis : en haut une sphère portant les points marqués $1$, $0$, $\infty$ et $\alpha$ (ce dernier cerclé), coupée par un grand cercle presque vertical, dont la moitié arrière est en tirets, et par un équateur ; à gauche, plus bas, un ovale étroit dont un bord est en tirets, dans un contour plus large à peine tracé, marqué $\alpha_0$ ; en bas une sphère dont l'équateur porte $0$, $1$ et, à l'arrière, $\infty$, chacun relié au pôle par un arc.
drawings.kind: three pencil sketches: two spheres with marked points, an oval
drawings.notes: The sheet is upside down in the scan (his writing runs the other way from the printed listing); the crop is turned by 180 degrees and the sketches are redrawn upright. Top: the sphere (outline as one closed curve; he went over it twice), the equator drawn as its front arc, the nearly vertical great circle (left half full, right half dashed), the points 1 (upper left), 0 (upper right), infinity (on the equator, right of the great circle) and alpha (ringed, at the left end of the equator), a thin line from the point 1 to the great circle carrying two small points, the stroke from alpha to the point 1, an arc on the right from the top through 0 down to the bottom, and two small crosses. Left: the narrow oval (right edge dashed), the wider faint contour round it, and the label alpha_0. Bottom: the sphere, its equator (an ellipse), the pole with a tick above it, the points 0, 1 on the front of the equator and infinity at the back, and the three arcs from the pole. Left out: a fourth, very faint, unlabelled oval at the upper left of the crop; his formulas and the printed listing. Still differs: in the top sphere several faint pencil arcs inside the outline (between alpha, the great circle and the bottom) are not all drawn, and those that are drawn are a reading; the thin line through 1 and the two small points seems to go on faintly to 0 and to the right rim (not drawn); the left half of the great circle and the right arc are doubled in places (drawn once); outlines are smooth curves through read points. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: points and labels within 1 mm of the page; the lower outline of the bottom sphere raised 3 mm and the upper left strand of the great circle moved 1.5 mm right, where they stand. The transcription's note says « le pôle $\infty$ » for the third sphere: on the page infinity sits on the back of the equator and the pole is unlabelled. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan (250 ppi native) on a unit grid, the crop turned 180 degrees; the three sketches lie on their pencil to within 1 to 2 units, as found on 12 November, so the redraw is unchanged. Not compiled (no TeX in the session). Still differs, as before: several faint arcs inside the top sphere are not all drawn; the thin line through 1 seems to go on faintly (not drawn); the doubled strokes of the great circle and the right arc are drawn once; a fourth, very faint oval at the upper left is left out.
drawings.orientation: sheet upside down in the scan: crop rotated by 180 degrees, drawn upright

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, à hauteur du passage encadré : un arc descendant qui fait un coin en un point marqué (le point $x$), un ovale en tirets autour de ce point, avec une croix à l'intérieur, et à droite du coin une région hachurée entre une corde et un arc.
drawings.kind: arc with a corner at a marked point, dashed neighbourhood, hatched region
drawings.notes: As on the page: the arc comes down from the upper right, makes a small step, turns back to a heavy point at the tip of a wedge (the point x of the lemma), and goes on downwards; round the point a dashed oval, which he left open on the right where the hatched region begins, with a small cross inside it at the lower left; right of the wedge a region bounded by the arc and by a second arc that leaves it at the top and rejoins it at the bottom, hatched by four oblique strokes (the first inside the wedge). Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the straight vertical stroke of the earlier redraw is not on the page (it was one of the hatching strokes) and was removed; the hatching is now his four strokes, not a pattern; the dashed oval follows his dashes and stays open on the right, as drawn. The transcription's note says « un point $x$ sur un arc, un voisinage en pointillé, une rive hachurée »: agreed, save that the letter x is not written by the sketch (a cross stands inside the oval). Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, au bas de la page : un arc ondulé qui descend et s'arrête en un point marqué, au milieu d'un disque au contour interrompu ; une croix sous le point.
drawings.kind: arc ending at a marked point inside a disc
drawings.notes: As on the page: a wavy arc coming down from above and ending at a heavy point inside a disc; the outline of the disc is drawn by him in six separate strokes (two short ones at the top, a short one at the upper left, a long one on the left, one along the bottom, a long one on the right) and they are drawn as he left them, gaps included; a small cross just under the end point (his mark for x). Nothing left out. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the dashed ellipse of the earlier redraw replaced by his six strokes, which do not lie on one ellipse; the lower part of the wavy arc (which swings left and back before the point) and the cross traced again. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, en regard du premier « Lemme 3 » barré, deux croquis. En haut, deux segments presque horizontaux l'un sous l'autre, chacun portant un point marqué vers son milieu et terminé à droite par un point noté « $1$ », hachurés l'un au-dessus, l'autre au-dessous (deux demi-plans), et une flèche verticale du premier au second. En bas, un demi-disque dont le diamètre porte un point marqué, d'où part un arc ondulé qui rejoint le demi-cercle.
drawings.kind: two sketches: two hatched half-planes glued along their edges; half-disc cut by an arc
drawings.notes: Top: the two edges, each drawn between its end points with the marked point computed on it; hatching above the upper edge (five oblique strokes and a short faint one, standing a little above the edge, as on the page) and below the lower one (seven strokes, the last short and apart); the end points and the two labels 1; the vertical arrow from the upper to the lower edge. Bottom: the diameter, the half-circle through its two ends, the heavy point on the diameter and the wavy arc from it to a point of the half-circle; a small hook under the point. Left out: the three long oblique strokes that strike the first « Lemme 3 » and cross the upper sketch (one of them crosses the upper edge at its left end); the words of the text at the right. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw had taken that striking stroke for a hatching stroke and had five evenly spaced strokes on each side; the hatching is now traced stroke by stroke, and the left side of the half-circle and the wavy arc were brought onto the page (1 to 3 mm). Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

figures.what: two hatched half-planes and an arrow

drawings.description: en haut à gauche, sous les mots écrits en biais : une courbe fermée, un point $b$ sur elle, en haut à droite ; de $b$ part vers l'intérieur un arc épais qui s'arrête en un point $a$, et vers l'extérieur deux branches marquées $\zeta$ et $\bar\zeta$ ; à l'intérieur, en bas, une petite flèche courbe d'orientation.
drawings.kind: closed curve with a boundary point b, an inner arc to a and two outer branches
drawings.notes: As on the page: the closed curve C as one closed curve through points read on his outline; the point b on it, where the arc I leaves the outline; the arc I from b inwards to its end point a (heavy in its lower half), labelled a; the two short branches outside, the left one labelled zeta and the right one zeta-bar; the small curved arrow inside, near the bottom. The branches do not start from b: the zeta stroke comes down to the blot left of b and stops there, about 3.5 mm from b; the zeta-bar stroke comes down to the outline about 4.5 mm right of b, above the second blot; they are drawn so. Left out: the marginal « NB … » written obliquely across the upper left of the curve, the two blots he made beside b (overwritten marks, perhaps heads of the two branches), and the title « Lemme 4 ». Still differs: the upper left of the outline is hidden under the oblique writing and is interpolated; the letters C and I are not written on the figure (the transcription's note names the curve and the arc after the text). Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw made all four strokes meet at one point b; the branches now end where they end on the page, b and the start of I were moved up 1.7 mm onto the outline, and the outline right of b was moved 1.5 mm out. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan (250 ppi native) on a unit grid; the closed curve, b, the thick arc to a, the two branches zeta and zeta-bar where they end and the small curved arrow lie on their ink to within about 1 unit, as found on 12 November, so the redraw is unchanged. Not compiled (no TeX in the session). Still differs: the upper left of the outline is hidden under the oblique writing and is interpolated; the two blots beside b (overwritten marks) are not drawn.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, à hauteur de B) : un cercle dont le bord porte trois petits traits marqués $\zeta$ (en haut à gauche), $1$ (à droite) et $\bar\zeta$ (en bas à gauche), et les trois arcs qu'ils découpent, notés $\alpha$ (à gauche), $\beta$ (en haut à droite) et $\bar\beta$ (en bas).
drawings.kind: circle with three marked points and the three arcs named
drawings.notes: As on the page: the circle as one closed curve through points read on his outline (taller than wide, flattened at the lower right), with the overshoot of the stroke where it closes at the bottom, which runs on below the outline for about 3 cm; three short ticks across it at the points zeta (upper left), 1 (right) and zeta-bar (lower left), each where he drew it, and the names of the three arcs written inside the circle next to each arc: alpha at the left, beta at the upper right, beta-bar at the bottom. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the fitted ellipse of the earlier redraw was up to 4 mm off at the bottom and the lower right; the outline is now traced, the overshoot drawn, the tick at 1 and the labels 1 and beta-bar moved 2 to 3 mm down, the tick at zeta-bar set where it stands. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en haut à gauche : un cercle, son centre marqué d'un petit rond noté $0$, et un arc ondulé qui va du centre au point du bord noté $1$, à droite.
drawings.kind: disc with a wavy arc from the centre to the boundary point 1
drawings.notes: As on the page: the circle as one closed curve through points read on his outline, with the two short overshoots of his stroke (at the lower right and at the bottom); a small full point near the centre with the label 0 just under it (his small round), the wavy arc from that point to the circle at the right (it first rises in a small hook, then runs nearly level in small waves), with a short tick there and the label 1 outside. Nothing left out. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the exact circle of the earlier redraw was up to 2 mm off his outline and its wavy arc missed the hook at the start; both traced again, the overshoots added. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: feuillet de dessins, sans un mot ni une formule : neuf sphères tracées à main levée au feutre (noir, brun, vert, orange, bleu), chacune découpée par un réseau d'arcs de grands cercles en régions dont certaines sont hachurées ou coloriées ; la plus grande, en orange, en haut à droite, est coupée par quatre cordes en secteurs, l'un hachuré
drawings.kind: page of spheres cut by great circles (coloured felt pens)
drawings.notes: Drawn on a computer printout; the printout text is left out. Nine spheres at their places on the sheet, each outline an ellipse and every chord ending exactly on its outline (endpoints projected onto it), crossings computed: 1 (left) shaded all over, with its network of wavy arcs; 2 (top centre) two chords crossing, the cap above their crossing hatched, a dashed arc behind; a small closed contour beside it; 3 (centre) two chords crossing, the top cap hatched, a dashed arc; 4 (top right, the largest) four chords, the sector between three of them hatched, with a line running down from it to sphere 9; 5 (bottom left, small) two chords and an arc; 6 a network of chords and arcs meeting at a point near the bottom; 7 two crossing chords and two arcs; 8 (thin outline) a vertical chord, two crossing chords, a hatched triangle with a marked point, a heavy arc on the right; 9 (thin outline) eight curved spokes from one point, a small hatched triangle at it, a marked point, a heavy arc on the right. Still differs: the felt-pen colours are not visible on the grey facsimile available here and are not rendered (the description names black, brown, green, orange, blue); the networks inside spheres 1 and 6 are approximate; arcs of great circles are drawn as chords or as smooth curves. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the facsimile is in colour when rendered without the grey option: sphere 1 is filled blue-green with a black network; spheres 2, 3 and 6 and the small contour are brown; the large sphere 4 with its chords, hatching and the line running down from it is orange; sphere 5 has a brown outline and chords with orange and blue-green arcs; sphere 7 has brown chords and an outline gone over in orange and blue-green, with an orange and a blue-green arc across it; spheres 8 and 9 are in a thin dark pen with a heavy orange arc on the right. The redraw now carries these colours (orange, brown, blue-green), one colour per stroke; where an outline is in two colours (spheres 5 and 7) it is drawn in one, and no green or blue distinct from the blue-green is seen. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan (250 ppi native) on a unit grid; the nine spheres and their coloured strokes lie on their ink to within 1 to 2 units for the outlines and most chords, so the redraw is unchanged. Not compiled (no TeX in the session). Still differs, as before: the networks inside spheres 1 and 6 and several chords of the large orange sphere are approximate (2 to 3 units); arcs of great circles are drawn as chords or smooth curves; where an outline is in two colours it is drawn in one.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, à hauteur de « fondamentaux » : un petit carré, sans lettres.
drawings.kind: small square, unlabelled
drawings.notes: A small square drawn free-hand in four separate strokes, with no letter, drawn as he left them: the top side and the right side meet at the upper right corner; the right side stops about 5 mm above the bottom side, with a small hook to the left; the left side starts below the left end of the top side and ends in a small hook; the bottom side starts right of the left side and stops short of the right side. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw closed the square; the open corners are now drawn as on the page. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, sous la note « $j = \tfrac12\log a$ ? » : un hexagone, sans lettres, avec son axe vertical, qui dépasse en haut et en bas, et la diagonale horizontale qui joint ses deux sommets latéraux.
drawings.kind: hexagon with its vertical axis and a horizontal diagonal
drawings.notes: As on the page: the hexagon (two horizontal sides, two lateral vertices), every side drawn between the same six vertices; the horizontal diagonal through the two lateral vertices, overshooting the right one a little, and a short dash of it left of the left vertex; the vertical axis through the middles of the two horizontal sides, overshooting below, and above up to a heavy point at its top; the bottom side running on past its right end, thinner, for about 9 mm. On the page the oblique sides are gone over several times (the two right ones as fans of three or four strokes, which do not quite reach the right lateral vertex) and the vertical axis is two strokes, the lower one about 2 mm left of the upper; each is drawn once. No letters on the figure. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: positions within 1.5 mm; added the heavy point at the top of the axis, the run-on of the bottom side and the dash left of the diagonal, and the diagonal now starts where he started it. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, à hauteur du cas $n = 4$ : un carré posé sur ses deux axes, tracés en tirets et qui le dépassent, avec deux flèches issues du centre vers les deux sommets du haut, notés $e_{1}$ (à gauche) et $e_{0}$ (à droite) ; au-dessus, deux traits obliques, l'un plein, l'autre en tirets, qui montent des sommets du haut vers le haut de l'axe vertical.
drawings.kind: square on its axes with the vectors e_0, e_1 from the centre
drawings.notes: As on the page: the square, its four sides between the same four corners; the two axes through the centre, dashed, overshooting the square (the horizontal one on both sides, the vertical one above, up to the top of the oblique strokes, and below, where it ends in a heavy stroke across the bottom side); further down, a small cross on the line of the vertical axis; two arrows from the centre to the upper left and upper right corners, labelled e_1 and e_0 (the left arrow starts a little above and left of the right one, as on the page); above the square, a full stroke (gone over twice, as a thin loop) from near the upper left corner to the top of the vertical axis and a dashed stroke from that top towards the upper right corner (the upper half of the square on the diagonals). Still differs: whether the two oblique strokes above are meant as two sides of a second square is not decided; the dashes of the axes are schematic; the left side is doubled at its lower end on the page (drawn once). Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the small cross was 11 mm too low in the earlier redraw and the horizontal axis 2 mm too low and 10 mm too long on the right; both corrected, and the feet of the two arrows set where they are. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan (250 ppi native) on a unit grid, corrected at 12 px per unit and laid over it again; not compiled (no TeX in the session). Changed: the square is not closed on the page: its four sides are four separate faint strokes with gaps at the corners, and the left side is doubled at its lower end; they are drawn so, each from where it starts to where it ends; the two arrows from the centre end in their heads just inside the upper corners (they were drawn to the corners, 2 units off); the full oblique stroke is drawn as the thin loop it is (gone over twice) and the dashed one from where its dashes start to where they end. The axes, the cross below and the labels e_1, e_0 lie on their ink to within about 1 unit; the dashes of the axes are drawn as a dash pattern, not dash by dash. Whether the two oblique strokes are two sides of a second square is a question of meaning, not of the drawing. Status set to ok.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, à hauteur du cas hexagonal : un hexagone de sommets notés $v - u$, $v$, $u$, $u - v$, $-v$, $-u$, avec six flèches du centre vers les sommets, et au-dessus du côté du haut un triangle dont le sommet est noté $2v - u$.
drawings.kind: hexagon with named vertices, arrows from the centre, outer triangle with apex 2v-u
drawings.notes: As on the page, stroke by stroke: the six sides of the hexagon are six separate strokes that stop short of the vertices (gaps of 2 to 5 mm at the corners; the upper right side ends in a small hook); the six arrows start a little away from the centre, each on its own, and end with their heads near the vertices; the two sides of the outer triangle are two strokes from near the vertices v-u and v that stop short of the top side and of each other (the right one ends in a hook); the seven labels where he wrote them (2v-u above the apex; v-u and v at the top; -u and u at the left and right; -v and u-v at the bottom). Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw joined every stroke at six computed vertices and drew the arrows from one centre to the vertices; on the page nothing is joined, so each stroke is now drawn where it stands. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, sous le mot « Démonstration » : l'hexagone, sommets notés $v - u$ et $v$ en haut, $-u$ à gauche, « $e_{0} = u_{+}$ » à droite (au bout d'une flèche épaisse issue du centre, sous laquelle est écrit $e_{0}$), $-v$ et « $\sigma v = u - v$ » en bas ; au-dessus, le sommet du triangle extérieur, noté « $2v - u = u_{-}$ » après un mot biffé ; des traits et des flèches vont du centre aux sommets, un axe vertical en tirets descend du sommet du triangle au centre.
drawings.kind: hexagon with named vertices, arrows from the centre, outer apex u_-
drawings.notes: As on the page, stroke by stroke (nothing is joined at computed vertices: on the page the strokes stop short of each other): the two sides of the outer triangle, the left one a plain stroke from above the vertex v-u towards the apex, the right one an arrow from near v up to the apex, the two stopping short of each other under « 2v-u = u_- »; the dashed vertical axis from the apex down to the centre, interrupted by the struck sign; the faint dashed middle part of the top side; the plain stroke from v-u down to the centre; the arrow from below -u up to v-u (the left upper side, with its head at v-u); the level stroke from -u towards the centre, stopping 8 mm short of it; the arrow from the centre to -v; a short stroke of the lower left side; the bottom side (gone over twice, drawn once); the arrow from the centre to u-v; the lower right side, stopping short of u-v; the heavy arrow from the centre to e_0 = u_+, with e_0 written under it; the right upper side from below v to e_0; the plain stroke from the centre towards v, stopping short of it. Labels where he wrote them. Left out: the struck word before « 2v-u », a struck sign inside the triangle, a short dashed vertical under v, and the word « Démonstration » above. Still differs: a small mark shaped like a 7 just below-left of v may be the head of the stroke from the centre towards v (not drawn); the top side is drawn only where its dashes can be seen; the label at the upper right vertex is overwritten and is given after the transcription as v. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop on 2026-11-12: the earlier redraw closed the hexagon and the triangle at computed vertices, drew every spoke from one centre to the vertices and had arrowheads on the wrong strokes (none on the arrow to the apex and the arrow to v-u, which carry them); redrawn stroke by stroke from the page. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): rasterised from its own coordinates over the 400 dpi colour scan (250 ppi native) on a unit grid; the strokes of the hexagon and of the outer triangle, the arrows from the centre and the labels lie on their ink to within about 1 unit, as redrawn on 12 November, so the redraw is unchanged. Not compiled (no TeX in the session). Still differs: the small 7-shaped mark below-left of v (perhaps the head of the stroke towards v) is not drawn; the top side is drawn only where its dashes can be seen; the overwritten label at the upper right vertex is given after the transcription as v.
